stanzaStarts: For even saints may turn aside
O’er rugged cliffs, and mountains high,
Why should we fear, though cowards say
Fear not, though life should be at stake,
We here may sometimes suffer wrong,
What though by some who seem devout,
Be steadfast, and with courage hold
O, let your hearts and hands be pure,
With patience cultivate within
Then let the “Times and Seasons” fly,
From her wide territorial wing
All earthly thrones are tottering things
But still her sceptre is approv’d—
But lo! a prize possessing more
That GIFT, however fools deride,
O would she now her influence bend—
Thus with the glory of her name
Though over millions call’d to reign—
For there are crowns and thrones on high,
Truth echoes—’tis Jehovah’s word;
The time, the time is now at hand
PART FIRST.
Slumb’ring Muse, can aught inspire thee
Is there aught can break thy slumbers—
While the twilight brown advances;
While yon peerless orb is shining
While earth’s care-worn sons, retiring,
While gay Pleasure’s children loiter,
While the city bustle ceases;
While the scenery’s fondly aiding
While the holiest thoughts invite thee,
PART SECOND.
I awake, I awake to the hallowed sound
’Tis a silken shackle that often binds
It was friendship too that boldly stood
Yes, friendship’s a sacred, a holy thing,
But hark! sweet music salutes my ear!
PART THIRD.
Spirit of Love, O whither
Amid the incongruities
In that dark vale of sorrow—
Amid the deep perplexities
Amid the rude commotions,
’Mid all its wild absurdities,
PART FOURTH.
Fair sons of light, that little world
Yet many noble spirits there,
Some of a high celestial birth,
And while their brief existence fills,
While others spurn my proffer’d hand,
The warmth that from my vitals springs
For them I search’d the highest heaven,
That man hereafter may again
Eternal beauties in thy features glow,
Let the fierce tigress chide her churlish brood;
But Truth! thy advocate shall not descend
Should lofty Genius strike a feeble string;
Go forth, and conquer—all to thee shall bow,
Victorious Truth! the conqu’ring scepter wield
Where is the Year? Envelop’d in the past,
The Year is gone! None but Omnipotence
But who, with common sense and eye unclos’d—
A few more years of hurried scenery

epigraphLines: “And when he had opened the fifth seal, I saw under the altar, the souls of them that were slain for the word of God, and for the testimony which they held.

stanzaStarts: Had nature’s self a heart, her heart would bleed
Oh! Illinois! thy soil has drank the blood
Once lov’d America! what can atone
Oh wretched murd’rers! fierce for human blood!
Shades of our patriotic fathers! Can it be,
’Twas not for crime or guilt of theirs, they fell—
Where are thy far-fam’d laws—Columbia! Where
Great men have fall’n and mighty men have died—
Oh, persecution! shall thy purple hand
Thou God of Jacob, in this trying hour
We mourn thy Prophet, from whose lips have flow’d
Now Zion mourns—she mourns an earthly head:
All hearts with sorrow bleed, and ev’ry eye
Ye Saints! be still, and know that God is just—
When the shafts of injustice were pointed at HIM—
When around you like hailstones, the rifle balls flew—
All the SCARS from your WOUNDS, like the trophies of yore

O Lord, my parents here preserve,
And, like the faithful ones of old,

Long may I sing thy praises here

headingLines: on the Death of Her Little One
stanzaStarts: A fondly cherish’d, tender flow’r—
That lovely babe, so sweet and fair—
That child is not within the tomb—
“Dust unto dust,” the earth receives
Her noble spirit deign’d to come,
Combin’d with rich matter, its elegant style,
I accept the fair gift, the rich, beautiful boon,
Haste, O haste, construct a Railway,
Infant Utah, strong in effort,
We shall be no longer outcasts

headingLines: Counselor to President Brigham Young
stanzaStarts: He’s not dead: He has laid his mortality by,
We miss him—we miss him: but why should we mourn?
He was prudent and wise—he was true to his trust—
As a friend—as a brother, we lov’d him well;

headingLines: One of the Twelve Apostles
stanzaStarts: You recognize as word of God,
A representative you go,
The steadfast course you have pursued
The sword was reeking from the sheath—
God gave them vict’ry o’er their foes,
That flag in stars and glory grew
Our fathers died: Their sons forgot
But lo! a phenix from the grave
A people with their all at stake,
Our Constitution too; all hail—

headingLines: thou hast with thee” [To Leonora Taylor]
stanzaStarts: Though Warriors bold, and Heroes true
’Tis all we ask this one request
We know thou wilt, we still believe
Full many a friend remaining here
Yes we shall still remembered be
Let Christians rage—they’d better hush
Then Though we know thou hast with thee
Of God our Father, may we here be blest,
The social circle proffer’d to bestow
But to the Saints, God will all things restore,
We now are strangers—pilgrims here below,
If, on this step-stone to another sphere,
You all are stewards of what you possess:
The infant mind is like an empty cell,
Will ignorance—will wit and sportive glee—
Your sons as heralds, soon must go abroad
Would not your bowels of compassion yearn
And very soon your blooming daughters will
Then, let your children be well taught in youth,

headingLines: Delivered by Eliza R. Snow, Jan. 9, 1855,

stanzaStarts: Hosanna to God: Let his praises abound
Like rich clusters of grapes on a desolate plain,
But the eye hath not seen, and the ear hath not heard,
Lo! The powers of the earth are beginning to shake,
And how blest are the saints who’re permitted to come
In eternal progression we’re taught to believe,
Father Adam, our God, let all Israel extol,
Much, much is learned by contrast. Who would know
The school of God impresses lessons well:
All things existing, will to good conduce,

Great Salt Lake City, Jan. 30, 1855
stanzaStarts: When last assembled, woman’s worth and sphere
I have apologies to offer here
No more of this. I’ll speak of woman now
And what is woman’s calling? where her place?
Hers is a holy calling, and her lot
That there are rights and privileges too,
Let woman then, a course in life pursue
Wit, youth, and beauty oft a charm impart
As we move forward to a perfect state
But ere this renovating work is thro’,
What we experience here, is but a school

stanzaStarts: She serv’d the God of Israel
She sooth’d the heart of sorrow,
She sought the poor and lowly,
Her mind was deck’d with knowledge,
Though from the cup of sorrow
She’s gone—and while we mourn her,
She fill’d her earthly mission
The Press—the Press—where th’ Press is free,
The Press—the Press—the Deseret Press—

headingLines: Delivered by Eliza R. Snow, February 6th, 1855,

in L. Snow’s Hall
Address by E. R. Snow, Feb. 27th, 1855,
before an Assembly of the “Polysophical Institution,”
in L. Snow’s Hall
stanzaStarts: One might as well my thoughts exterminate—
Not all the charms surrounding scenes impart
But where—O where the land so choice—so dear?
Nor would I boast a proud nativity—
Nor yet in Germany, where laws are made
Not Britain with her mountains, hills, and dales,
Not Sweden, Denmark, Norway—not in France
Neither America’s much favor’d land,
I say, with brother Eddington: I’m not
The noblest spirits scatter’d o’er the earth,
One God—one faith—one baptism: we are now
The Holy Spirit, ev’ry saint receives
That is the charm—the nationality—
As foreign trav’lers, each a camping ground
Our hearts beat upward and our spirits move

headingLines: Written for, and Read before
the Polysophical Institution
March 19, 1855, in the Hall of L. Snow
stanzaStarts: As I was musing with desire intense
“What wouldst thou me?” the seraph gently said:
With firm, attentive mind—with list’ning ear
But then the more immediate cause of this
This earth’s your Father’s workshop: what is done—
Then shame, O shame on all the strife you see
It will not matter whatsoever’s gain’d
As disobedience fill’d the world with pain,
Then list to me—my precepts all obey;
Adam, your God, like you on earth has been
Obedience will the same bright garland weave
Life’s ultimatum unto those that live
Thus said the seraph:—Sacred in my heart
I felt my littleness, and thought, henceforth
As thus I mused, the lovely queen of night
We find a radius in the soul,
The blessed prescience God has given
All pain and grief to pleasure tend—
That restless thing, anxiety,
Compared with past life—life before,
But ’tis as God ordained to be,
And when I’m all in all resigned—
To me, it matters little now,
I war for Zion—not for me:
I glimpse at data far behind
But now I’m a child of dust;
Adam, our father—Eve, our mother,
Then, Sister, what—O, what this life—
I know how bitter portions taste,
Fear not, my Sister: God is just,
How blest to be on Zion’s ship!
Unwisely and untimely sought,
Training the mind to circumstances
But O, that glorious day of rest,
We may sacrifice friends and relations,
Of the cup of this life’s deepest sorrow,
We may bask in the Spirit’s bright visions—
With our might, we may seem to be doing,
For we all are requir’d to surrender,
Some would even choose sooner t’ extinguish
Yet our labor, our tithings and offerings
Though we keep every other commandment,
Tho’ we pass over Seas Of Affliction
Very small it may be in appearance—
This is a dispensation rife with change:
The hurried motions of all things portend
A preparation speedily must be
The “Polysophic Institute” will now
Then brethren go: yes, go, and be you blest—
Keep mem’ry’s mirror clear—’twill thus recall

The great day of the Lord is approaching,

stanzaStarts: Tho’ your pathway in life has been lone and drear,
Our great Father’s law is the law of love,
The God whom we worship, is wise and just;

The dark vail of obscurity round us—
But the vail from the mind will be taken—
With good and evil—right and wrong,
If there are given rules, by which

headingLines: on His Departure for Europe
stanzaStarts: You leave the Vales of Ephraim—
You’re going from the nurs’ry,
You leave the fount of knowledge,
Should evil powers surround you,
Touch not, taste not, nor handle,—
Go,—you will be remembered
Go—go, fulfil your Mission,
You go, salvation’s joyful sound
Tho’ hardships in your pathway lie—
Work, while the day of labor lasts
Go, Brother, go and never fear
You’ll not forget the household, where
Our mutual blessings on you rest
Then go in peace and be thou blest:

stanzaStarts: In this as well as ev’ry other land
And by the bye, to all I fain would say,
To our young friends I’ll give a key whereby
’Neath the perverted sceptre Mammon wields,
Not so in Zion—works and Godly fear
The Saints may sometimes suffer want, ’tis sure,
That heavenly foretaste of a glorious rest,

In Babylon, where money is the test,
Show me a Saint that’s poor, and once for all
Methink I hear one softly whisper, “Hush—
I boast of wealth and richer streams than flow
My Father’s rich—I am his lawful child—
Who are my friends? Your worthy selves, I trust,

Who is my brother? Israel’s Holy One—
And who is my Father? Is he wise and great,
Prov’d or not prov’d, this axiom is sure,
You’ll have wisdom and grace from the fountain of God
You have sipp’d the pure waters of life, and you know

Help us O Lord, to blend
Thy spirit is the charm

stanzaStarts: He needs no eulogy to speak his worth—

We know he’s gone! We feel it deeply too;
His earthly tenement lies folded in
Wake up, ye Saints, and be alive to God—
Keep humble in your spirit
Guard well the springs of action
Altho’ the way is narrow:
Tho’ for a little season,
What may have seem’d affliction,
Our Father had a purpose
In heav’n’s eternal councils,
You’ve represented Adam
Your course is onward, upward,
Bright with celestial fulness,

headingLines: to the Ladies of the United States Camp
in a Crusade against the ‘Mormons’
stanzaStarts: Has cruel persecution,
Have you been mob’d and plunder’d
No, no; you’ve join’d a crusade
Amid the dreary desert,
We never had intruded
We came through sore compulsion,
Can woman’s heart be callous
Should sickness prey upon you
We’re form’d of blood and sinews
We love with purer feelings
We have the ancient order
We’re well prepar’d to teach you,
We’d fain from human suff’ring
The Scriptures are fulfilling—
Whence comes it?—From the spicy grove
Or comes it from the rich saloon,
Or comes it from the blazing hearth,
Speak not of Ida’s towering height,
The Muse’s attic numbers swell,
’Tis not for carnage—not for blood—
The will of God, those brave men know,
They serve the God of battles, and
That single line expresses more,
While union and obedience reign
To them, O Father, e’er dispense
Not in their proudest, manliest hour,
And yet a test—a test is near,
That song—all truthful songs are given
The spirit which at first inspired
Not unto us—but to the Lord,

The Church Historians labours to divide
Faithful to God and to your Brethren true
In that blest world where light and knowledge dwell
Fill’d with immortal majesty and might

Your civil pow’rs, your officers of State,
What have they done? O blush, humanity!
Here, in the mountains, ’neath the western sky,
Your noble, gen’rous heart, with pure intent,
We’ve sued for peace, and for our Rights, in vain:

Announce to Congress that the moon
Say too, the twinkling orbs of night
Tell Congress that the Seasons now,
Let Congress know, the orbs above
Or else announce one fact instead,

headingLines: [“Let those who would be Saints indeed”]
stanzaStarts: What though the storm-clouds gather dark?
Fear not the darkness of the night,
Sell not your birth-right for a mess
The wheat has clear’d the threshing floor—
And Zion’s furnace, too, will burn,
In His own time God will remove
Maintain the freedom you have won—
Your parentage—your kindred I have known
But Change, since then, has wrought with mighty hand,
What is this life? It is a transient thing—
The pruning time has come and we are here
Fear not the future nor regret the past—
A King in cog.—a God in embryo,
Your past experience will prove richer far

headingLines: [To Brother David and Sister Elizabeth Day]
stanzaStarts: For a while the cherub nestled
All the strength of warm affection—
Wait in hope, fond weeping parents;
God sent that lovely jewel
She fill’d her earthly mission—
She’s safe from earth’s corruption—

headingLines: Daughter of Jesse Smith
stanzaStarts: May peace and virtue crown her days,
May she in childhood, love to think,
May nature copiously confer,
Long may she live to fill her place
And when in faithfulness she’s shar’d
He has gone—the affectionate father—
How cruel the blow of bereavement!
Eternity’s vail may enfold him
He neither is dead nor a sleeping
He has enter’d a higher existence
Dear Sister, don’t cherish your sorrow;

headingLines: [To Miss Carmichael]
stanzaStarts: To Miss Carmichael, G. S. L. City.—
In the mirage and foam of fiction,
With truth we can bless the righteous—
Truth—truth is the soul of reason—
Crave not what the world calls honor—
Stoop not to Parnassian glories—
A holier muse will fire thee,
On, on, for the point before you
Those who salvation’s truth believe, but love to disobey—
Of all the apostle Paul endured, his perils were the worst,
Then marvel not ye demagogues, who’re making much ado,
We’ve females whose intelligence—whose loveliness and grace,
And we have men by God inspired, and clothed with power to bless—
High-toned in spirit—in their lives, they’re far above reproach;
We need no sails for Zion’s ship, our foes may pause and wonder—
Truth, peace, and equity will claim the prize, and win the day;

headingLines: [“Your sweet little rose bud has left you”]
stanzaStarts: Your babe in the grave is not sleeping,
They’ve treasures they’ve laid up in heaven
They’ve gone where life’s ills cannot find them—
Look up and you’ll find consolation
No: no, I answer no: your gifted pen
Eternal Wisdom and eternal Love
Then take the lyre and touch its chords again
There amidst its lights and shadows—
Change has wrought its revolutions
Since our future exaltation
Dwell not on the past, my brother,—
There, we have our all invested
Life’s open sea we must encounter—
Why should we mourn when youthful dust
Why sorrow if bold manhood’s term;
And wherefore grieve when hoary age
But when the deep, dark shade of crime
I never lov’d those scenes of gayety,
Give me the happy medium between
Pure social life, the holiest gem which heav’n
It gives him, too,
“Pearl of great price!” ’Tis worth all sacrifice
No matter what or how things come and go
It holds the heav’n-acknowledg’d claim on Truth—
The root the spring, the fountain or the head,
The trunk, to Christ, who is the living vine,
Again—We’ll thus compare the tree of life:
The leaves, the holy Prieshood, that will rest
And thus, will Joseph, Brigham, Heber too,
Though limb to limb, be grafted on, until
Christ is the holy Branch from Jesse’s root;
You see no cringing in his look—
He shows no tremor in his hand—
The same in person ev’rywhere,
The souls of gifts he can dispense;
His whisper reaches ev’ry ear
What mean those accents swelling high?
His finger on injustice laid,
He oft in worship bends the knee,
Who is this noble champion, who,
We have millions of years for improvement, yes, more;
I’m an every-day student. I’m taught by the bee—
Eternal progression! How glorious to think
And yet, with all its virtues—all its worth,
It oft is sacrific’d—’tis offer’d up
Let once the pillars that support its throne
SAINTS, with each other should pursue a course
Sweeter to me, than honey in the comb,
What God approves, I love. The confidence
Soothing as balmy evening zephyrs—sweet

Why should the implements of peace

headingLines: for the Opening of the Theater in Great Salt Lake City
stanzaStarts: In the midst of the mountains high crowning the West
’Twas by the great Jehovah’s hand
But shivering pal’sy seize th’ accursed arm
The Gods are free
Here in our mountain Deseret,
We hold the triple pow’r to feel
While these strong engines wisely are directed
There’s a God! He has spoken—His word is our law
The American Eagle expanded its crest
Truth is Zion’s royal Standard
With broad streamers on high in the clear azure sky
Hallelujah! God’s own kingdom
Hallelujah—hallelujah

headingLines: [“O God, bless Brigham Young”]

Bless all thy servants, Lord,
Long live the wise and just,
Long, long live Brigham Young,

headingLines: at the Celebration of Their Wedding—6 Years Ago
stanzaStarts: As you in life’s progressive journey go

With Time’s advance, let ev’ry step you take,
By sweet and bitter properly applied,

headingLines: on Their 16th Wedding Day Celebration
stanzaStarts: Sixteen years, your nuptial union
Confidence produces union—
God has blest your mutual efforts—
May your trust in God be strengthen’d
Of the pow’r of lives eternal
List, list not to the fickle strain
But heav’n has sent affection here
And of its genial pow’r possess’d,

But, hush! the Year’s successor boldly comes.
The tide of Time heaves up, and on its crest
A change—a change must come. Prophets declared
“It must be so,” for so has God decreed.

Where—where is now

But yet we feel, and deeply mourn the loss,

Sweet tones of pensive playfulness
When busy day, retiring,
’Tis now the morning twilight
He saw chaotic elements control’d—
He saw the curse with all its woe, entail’d
He’s seen huge empires creeping from the gulph
All this:—And he has not beheld a scene—
The conflict closely wag’d—and Oh!
From their high seats, cherubic hosts arose,
The Son of God, came off victorious:
‘Welcome, welcome, King of glory—
Thou art he who stoop’d to conquer—
Down to the dregs, thou didst not shrink

Glory to thee, we will repeat

It matters not what ills we may surmount,
And if we pattern from the bee,
Whate’er of the substance of earth we lay by,
If kings and queens we ever rise to be,
To study the dealings and ways of the Lord

What is life’s gaudy splendor—its pride and its show?
